title: Joining Benny Goodman's sextet in 1945 through Seven Lively Arts
summary: Goodman heard Stewart at the Three Deuces and asked him to fill in for his brother in the sextet at Seven Lively Arts; Stewart then joined him steadily.

story.theme_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the leader and his bands
story.community_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the perfectionist bandleader

blocks.x: When did you join Benny Goodman's band?
Oh, so this was like after --
I had come back closer to home, you know, New York City. I was working the Three Deuces.
That was when you were working with Tatum, Three Deuces?
And then -- was this around the time that Tatum got ill and you --
Yeah, this was the time when -- yeah.
So when you weren't working with your own band with Collins and West and Garner, that was when you went into Goodman's sextet.
Now, who all was in Goodman's sextet when you went in?

Well, now, at this particular time, Benny -- I was working at the Three Deuces with my group. In fact, if I'm not mistaken, it was either Billy Taylor or Beryl Booker with me and they -- here's what I was about to say. Benny Goodman's sextet was doing a show down the street from us on Sixth Avenue at one of the theaters -- I forget -- it was one of the theaters on Sixth Avenue, not far from the Three Deuces. It was a kind of a show they were playing for. It was called Seven Lively Arts and Benny Goodman was featured with his sextet, which with him, he had his brother, Harry Goodman, playing the bass and on guitar, Mike Bryan. On drums, he had Mory Feld and on vibraphones, he had Red Norvo and Teddy Wilson on piano. Somehow, Goodman had stopped into the Three Deuces to see our quartet. It was a nice meeting there. In fact, that was the first time I had ever met Benny Goodman and this particular night, Benny asked me, could I fill in with him, take his brother's place, because his brother had something else to do

and if I could take time off between my gig to come down and play. They did shows, one show per night, at the 'Seven Lively Arts,' and he asked me was there any way I could take off from my job and come down and play with him at this theater, which I finally did.

You should see me. I played one set at the club and I had to be at the theater before 10:00 to be ready for -- to go on stage with Benny. So my trio, my quartet, the other kids took over while I was gone and I did the show with Benny and then I had to rush back to my gig at the Three Deuces. So that is actually the first time I have had a beautiful experience playing with Benny Goodman, the sextet.

From there on out, I played with him -- after the show folded at the 'Seven Lively Arts' affair, Benny asked me would I work with him steady, you know, and it was about that time when my engagement at the Three Deuces was about to end anyway. So that's when I joined Benny on a steady basis, you know. That was the start of the happenings with Benny Goodman.
